item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the American Academy of Diplomacy Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship, an opportunity designed for students and recent graduates who want practical exposure to diplomacy, foreign affairs, communications and nonprofit management.

Based at the American Academy of Diplomacy, an organization whose membership includes former senior ambassadors and career diplomats, the programme offers an unusual opportunity to work closely with a small professional team while learning more about how diplomacy, foreign-policy engagement and nonprofit organizations function in practice.

Rather than limiting the intern to one narrow area of work, the Academy plans to involve the selected candidate across a wide range of organizational responsibilities. These include managing social-media accounts, helping implement events and meetings, communicating with Academy members, updating website content, maintaining contact lists, supporting professional staff and creating an independent project.

The Academy particularly encourages applications from a student or recent graduate with continuing education goals who has an interest in the Foreign Service, communications, nonprofit management or the broader practice of American diplomacy.

The internship requires a commitment of 20 to 40 hours per week, depending on the candidate’s availability. Applicants must also be able to participate for a minimum of 13 weeks. Candidates who cannot commit to at least 13 weeks will not be considered.

The programme is unpaid, although academic credit may be possible depending on the requirements of the participant’s school or university. The Academy reviews applications on a rolling basis, meaning interested candidates are encouraged to apply before the final deadline rather than waiting until the last day.

Application deadline: End of day on November 2, 2026.

About the American Academy of Diplomacy

The American Academy of Diplomacy, commonly referred to as the Academy or AAD, is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening the resources and tools the United States brings to managing diplomatic challenges.

Its work is aimed at improving understanding of the importance of diplomacy and increasing the effectiveness of American engagement with the international community.

The Academy pursues this mission through activities such as:

  • Targeted outreach programmes
  • Policy proposals
  • Publications
  • Distinguished awards
  • Professional engagement
  • Discussions on diplomacy and foreign policy

An important feature of the organization is its membership. The Academy is composed of former senior ambassadors and career diplomats who bring extensive professional experience in the practice of diplomacy.

For an intern, this creates a professional environment that is quite different from a conventional university internship. The selected candidate may have opportunities to interact with people who have spent significant portions of their careers working directly on diplomatic negotiations, international relations, foreign-policy implementation and overseas representation.

About the Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship

The Academy is specifically looking for an individual interested in two connected areas:

  1. The practice of American diplomacy; and
  2. The internal workings of a nonprofit organization.

Because the Academy is a relatively small organization, it states that an intern can become an integral part of its core team.

This matters because internships at larger institutions can sometimes separate interns from central organizational work. At AAD, the selected intern is expected to contribute directly to the Academy’s regular communications, programme and administrative activities.

The opportunity may be especially relevant for students considering careers in:

  • Diplomacy
  • Foreign Service
  • International affairs
  • Strategic communications
  • Public diplomacy
  • Foreign-policy organizations
  • Think tanks
  • Nonprofit management
  • Public policy
  • Government affairs
  • International relations
  • Digital communications

However, the Academy does not require applicants to be enrolled in one specific academic major.

What Will the Intern Do?

The internship combines communications, programme support, event assistance, digital content management and organizational administration.

Managing the Academy’s Social Media Accounts

One of the most significant responsibilities is helping manage the Academy’s social-media presence.

The Academy specifically prefers applicants who have previous organizational experience using platforms such as:

  • X
  • LinkedIn
  • TikTok
  • Instagram
  • Facebook

Experience with social-media analytics is also considered valuable.

The selected intern may therefore be involved in activities such as preparing posts, promoting Academy publications, distributing articles written by Academy members, publicizing events and helping analyze audience engagement.

This could be especially useful for someone interested in digital diplomacy, strategic communications or public affairs, where institutions increasingly rely on social media to communicate policy ideas and professional expertise.

Supporting the Distribution of Academy Members’ Published Work

The Academy notes that interns may assist with distributing articles written by its distinguished members.

This could provide experience in identifying appropriate digital channels, preparing concise promotional copy and presenting foreign-policy analysis to wider audiences.

The work may help the intern develop skills in:

  • Editorial promotion
  • Social-media writing
  • Audience engagement
  • Digital communications
  • Content distribution

For students interested in journalism or public diplomacy, this part of the placement could provide valuable experience in translating substantive foreign-policy content into accessible public communications.

Helping With Events and Meetings

The intern will also assist with the organization and implementation of Academy events and meetings.

This may involve helping professional staff prepare for:

  • Committee meetings
  • Board meetings
  • Public events
  • Member activities
  • Policy discussions
  • Other Academy programmes

The internship description specifically mentions assisting during committee and Board meetings as an example of the level of responsibility an intern may receive.

This means organizational ability and attention to detail will be important.

An intern may need to keep track of schedules, documents, participants, communications and follow-up tasks without constant supervision.

Communicating With Academy Members

The selected intern will interact with Academy members as part of regular organizational operations.

Because the Academy’s membership includes experienced diplomats and former ambassadors, communication needs to be accurate and professional.

The Academy explicitly expects a successful intern to be detail-oriented enough to handle tasks such as sending member emails without constant guidance.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate an ability to communicate professionally through:

  • Email
  • Written correspondence
  • Digital platforms
  • Internal organizational communications

A strong command of written English is particularly important.

Updating the Academy Website

The intern will help update content on the Academy’s website.

The Academy indicates that front-end Wix development experience is preferred, although it is not listed as an absolute requirement.

Applicants who already have experience using Wix may therefore have an advantage.

Candidates who have worked with other content-management systems may also have transferable experience. Examples could include:

  • WordPress
  • Squarespace
  • Drupal
  • Other web publishing systems

The role does not appear to require advanced software development. The emphasis is on front-end website and content-management capability.

Managing Contact Lists

The intern will help manage organizational contact lists.

This can involve maintaining accurate information about:

  • Academy members
  • Event participants
  • Professional contacts
  • Mailing lists
  • Other institutional stakeholders

Although this may appear to be a simple administrative responsibility, accurate database management is essential in a membership organization.

The Academy therefore emphasizes the importance of being detail-oriented.

Supporting Professional Staff

The intern will provide broader support to the Academy’s professional staff.

Because the organization is small, interns may be exposed to several dimensions of nonprofit management at the same time.

This could help participants learn more about:

  • Programme coordination
  • Administrative systems
  • Institutional communications
  • Membership organizations
  • Foreign-policy programming
  • Event management
  • Digital outreach

This broad exposure may be particularly useful for students who are still determining which professional path within international affairs most interests them.

Create Your Own Project

Another notable component of the internship is the opportunity to create an independent project.

The Academy does not prescribe one specific project that every intern must complete.

This can potentially allow the selected participant to develop something that reflects both organizational priorities and their own professional interests.

Depending on discussions with the Academy, such a project could potentially involve subjects such as:

  • Digital communications
  • Diplomacy outreach
  • Social-media strategy
  • Membership engagement
  • Website content
  • Communications analytics
  • Foreign-policy resources

Applicants should not assume that any particular project will automatically be approved, but thinking about a possible contribution before applying could strengthen an interview or cover letter.

Mentorship and Professional Guidance

The Academy states that its Program and Finance Assistant will provide detailed guidance and constructive critique.

The purpose is to maximize the intern’s learning experience.

This means the programme is intended to have a developmental component rather than simply assigning administrative tasks without feedback.

A participant may therefore gain experience receiving professional critique and improving their work in areas such as:

  • Writing
  • Communications
  • Organization
  • Programme support
  • Professional judgment

Weekly Time Commitment

The intern is expected to devote:

20 to 40 hours per week

to the programme.

The precise weekly commitment can depend on the selected intern’s availability.

This gives some flexibility for students balancing the internship with academic responsibilities, although even the lower end of 20 hours per week represents a substantial professional commitment.

Candidates should therefore carefully consider their academic timetable before applying.

Minimum Internship Duration

Applicants must be available for at least:

13 weeks.

This is a firm condition.

The Academy clearly states that applicants who cannot dedicate a minimum of 13 weeks to the programme will not be considered.

When applying, candidates should therefore ensure that their proposed start and end dates cover at least this period.

Is the Internship Paid?

No.

The Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship is unpaid.

The Academy explicitly states that participation is without compensation.

Applicants should therefore consider their financial circumstances before applying, particularly if participation would require:

  • Transportation
  • Housing
  • Relocation
  • Other living expenses

The announcement does not identify any stipend, travel support, accommodation allowance or relocation funding.

Does the Internship Lead to Employment?

No employment is guaranteed.

The Academy specifically states that participating in the programme comes without an expectation of employment at the conclusion of the internship.

Applicants should therefore view this primarily as a learning and professional-development opportunity rather than a guaranteed pathway into a paid position at AAD.

Academic Credit May Be Available

Although the internship is unpaid, academic credit may potentially be available.

Whether a student can obtain credit depends on the rules of their school or university.

Interested students should therefore consult their:

  • Academic department
  • Internship coordinator
  • Career centre
  • Faculty adviser

to determine whether the internship can count toward their academic programme.

The Academy itself does not guarantee that every institution will award credit.

Requirements for a Successful Internship Experience

The Academy identifies several qualities and skills it considers important.

Interest in Nonprofit Work

Applicants should have a genuine interest in nonprofit organizations.

The Academy is not a government agency, although its subject matter is closely connected to diplomacy and foreign policy.

Understanding the difference between a nonprofit policy organization and a government department may help applicants explain their motivation more effectively.

Interest in American Foreign Affairs or the Foreign Service

An interest in American foreign affairs and/or the U.S. Foreign Service is particularly desirable.

Candidates considering careers related to diplomacy may therefore find this programme especially relevant.

Relevant areas of academic or professional interest could include:

  • International relations
  • Political science
  • Diplomacy
  • Foreign policy
  • Public policy
  • Government
  • History
  • Communications
  • International studies

The Academy does not, however, state that applicants must study one of these subjects.

Previous Organizational Social Media Experience

The Academy prefers applicants who have experience managing social-media accounts for an organization.

Relevant experience could come from:

  • A university society
  • Student government
  • A nonprofit organization
  • A student newspaper
  • A previous internship
  • A volunteer organization
  • A professional association
  • A research centre

The preferred platforms include X, LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram and Facebook.

Experience working with social-media analytics is also desirable.

Candidates should therefore mention if they have worked with metrics such as:

  • Reach
  • Engagement
  • Impressions
  • Click-through rates
  • Audience growth
  • Post performance

Strong Attention to Detail

Attention to detail is one of the most important personal qualities emphasized by the Academy.

The intern may be trusted with activities such as member emails and Board or committee meeting support.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they are comfortable handling tasks where accuracy matters.

Examples might include:

  • Managing mailing lists
  • Editing publications
  • Coordinating events
  • Maintaining databases
  • Preparing official correspondence

Strong Writing Ability

Applicants should have strong writing skills and a firm command of:

  • Grammar
  • Spelling
  • Syntax

Because the internship includes communications and website work, writing quality is likely to be assessed throughout the application process.

Candidates should therefore carefully proofread both their résumé and cover letter.

An application containing obvious grammatical or spelling errors could weaken an otherwise strong candidacy.

Microsoft Office Proficiency

Applicants should be highly proficient in Microsoft Office.

The Academy specifically names:

  • Word
  • Access
  • Excel
  • PowerPoint

Candidates who have advanced skills in any of these programmes may want to describe them specifically rather than simply stating “Microsoft Office proficiency.”

Examples might include:

  • Excel spreadsheet management
  • PowerPoint presentation design
  • Access database management
  • Word document formatting

Gmail and Google Apps

High proficiency with Gmail and Google Apps is preferred.

Relevant experience may include:

  • Gmail
  • Google Docs
  • Google Sheets
  • Google Drive
  • Google Calendar
  • Google Forms

Applicants who have managed collaborative projects through Google Workspace may wish to highlight this experience.

Wix Experience

Front-end Wix development experience is preferred.

This requirement reflects the internship’s website-management responsibilities.

Applicants who have previously updated websites or designed pages using Wix should make this visible in their application.

Wix experience is described as preferred rather than mandatory.

Ability to Work Independently

The Academy wants someone who can complete responsibilities without needing constant supervision.

This is particularly important because small nonprofit teams often require staff and interns to take ownership of tasks.

Candidates should be able to:

  • Prioritize work
  • Meet deadlines
  • Ask appropriate questions
  • Solve routine problems
  • Complete assigned tasks independently

Ability to Work as Part of a Team

At the same time, the selected candidate must be able to collaborate effectively.

The intern will work with professional staff and communicate with Academy members.

Strong teamwork and professional interpersonal skills will therefore be important.

Friendly and Outgoing Personality

The Academy specifically states that it values someone who is:

  • Friendly
  • Outgoing
  • Equipped with a good sense of humor

This indicates that interpersonal fit is considered important alongside technical skills.

The intern may interact with senior diplomats, Academy staff and other professional stakeholders, making confidence and professionalism useful qualities.

Who Is Most Likely to Benefit From This Opportunity?

The internship may be especially valuable for students or recent graduates exploring careers in:

  • Diplomacy
  • Foreign Service
  • International relations
  • Foreign policy
  • Public diplomacy
  • Strategic communications
  • International nonprofit organizations
  • Think tanks
  • Government relations
  • Public affairs
  • Programme management
  • Digital communications

Someone interested in diplomacy but unsure whether they want to enter government service could also benefit from seeing how a nonprofit organization contributes to the foreign-policy ecosystem.

Application Process

Applications are submitted directly by email.

Candidates must send:

  • A résumé
  • A cover letter

to:

academy@academyofdiplomacy.org

The email subject line must be:

Academy Internship Application

Applicants should also include in the email:

  • Their schedule availability
  • Tentative internship start date
  • Tentative internship end date

The Academy asks applicants not to make phone calls regarding applications.

Application Deadline

Applications must be received by:

End of day, November 2, 2026.

However, this should not be interpreted as a reason to wait until November.

The Academy reviews applications on a rolling basis and specifically encourages candidates to apply early.

What Does Rolling Review Mean?

Rolling review means applications can be evaluated as they arrive rather than all being assessed only after the closing date.

Candidates who already have their materials ready may therefore benefit from submitting earlier.

Applicants should still prioritize quality over speed, but there is little advantage in deliberately waiting until the November 2 deadline.

How to Prepare a Strong Cover Letter

A strong cover letter should directly connect the candidate’s experience with the Academy’s needs.

Applicants may want to address four questions.

Why are you interested in diplomacy?

Explain why diplomacy, foreign policy or the Foreign Service interests you.

Avoid relying entirely on broad phrases such as “I am passionate about international relations.”

Concrete academic, professional or personal experiences can make the explanation more convincing.

Why are you interested in communications?

The internship contains substantial communications responsibilities.

Applicants should mention relevant experience with:

  • Writing
  • Social media
  • Website management
  • Journalism
  • Public engagement
  • Publications

What can you contribute?

The Academy is looking for someone who can contribute actively to its small team.

Applicants should identify practical skills such as:

  • Social-media management
  • Copywriting
  • Analytics
  • Event organization
  • Website editing
  • Research
  • Database management
  • Graphic design
  • Video editing

Why the American Academy of Diplomacy?

Applicants should demonstrate that they understand the organization.

A strong answer might connect the Academy’s membership of experienced diplomats, its nonprofit model and its focus on strengthening American diplomacy with the candidate’s own interests.

How to Prepare Your Résumé

Applicants should tailor their résumé specifically for the internship.

Relevant experience might include:

  • Student organizations
  • Model United Nations
  • Debate societies
  • International affairs clubs
  • Student journalism
  • Communications roles
  • Social-media management
  • NGO volunteering
  • Event coordination
  • Research assistantships
  • Website management
  • Administrative work

Candidates should describe results rather than only duties whenever possible.

For example, rather than writing:

“Managed social media.”

A stronger résumé might say:

“Managed LinkedIn and Instagram content for a university international-affairs society and tracked monthly engagement analytics.”

About the Academy’s Washington, DC Headquarters

The American Academy of Diplomacy lists its address as:

1101 17th Street NW, Suite 200
Washington, DC 20036
United States

The internship announcement itself does not clearly specify whether the Spring 2027 arrangement is fully on-site, hybrid or remote.

Applicants for whom location is a major consideration should therefore confirm the working arrangement directly with the Academy.

Do not assume remote participation is available unless the Academy confirms it.

Application Contact Information

American Academy of Diplomacy

1101 17th Street NW, Suite 200
Washington, DC 20036
United States

Internship application email:
academy@academyofdiplomacy.org

Official internship page:
https://www.academyofdiplomacy.org/internship-details

The Academy specifically requests no phone calls regarding internship applications.

Key Details at a Glance

Programme: Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship

Organization: American Academy of Diplomacy

Fields: Diplomacy, communications, nonprofit management, foreign affairs and programme support

Target applicants: Students and recent graduates with continuing education goals

Weekly commitment: 20–40 hours

Minimum duration: 13 weeks

Compensation: Unpaid

Academic credit: May be available depending on school requirements

Key responsibilities: Social media, events, meetings, member communications, website updates, contact-list management, staff support and an independent project

Preferred platforms: X, LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram and Facebook

Software: Microsoft Word, Access, Excel and PowerPoint required; Gmail/Google Apps and Wix preferred

Application materials: Résumé and cover letter

Application email: academy@academyofdiplomacy.org

Subject line: Academy Internship Application

Additional information to include: Schedule availability and tentative start/end dates

Review: Rolling basis

Deadline: End of day November 2, 2026

Conclusion

The American Academy of Diplomacy Spring 2027 Program & Communications Internship provides an opportunity for students and recent graduates to gain practical experience at the intersection of diplomacy, communications and nonprofit management.

Because the Academy is a small organization, the selected intern is expected to participate directly in its core activities rather than simply observe from the sidelines. Responsibilities can include managing social media, helping organize events and meetings, communicating with Academy members, maintaining contact lists, updating website content, supporting professional staff and developing an individual project.

The internship may be particularly attractive to candidates considering careers in diplomacy, the Foreign Service, international relations, strategic communications, public diplomacy, nonprofit management or foreign-policy organizations.

Applicants should have strong writing and organizational skills, familiarity with Microsoft Office and an ability to operate both independently and collaboratively. Previous organizational social-media experience is particularly relevant, while experience with Google Workspace, social-media analytics and Wix can further strengthen an application.

Candidates must commit at least 13 weeks and approximately 20 to 40 hours per week. The internship is unpaid, although academic credit may be possible depending on university requirements.

Because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, interested candidates should consider applying well before the final closing date.

Final application deadline: End of day, November 2, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Princeton in Asia (PiA) 2027-28 Fellowship Program, offering immersive, paid work opportunities with host organizations and communities across Asia. The program is designed for graduates who want to develop professionally while participating in meaningful cross-cultural exchange between the United States and Asia.

For the 2027-28 cycle, Princeton in Asia expects to offer approximately 60 fellowship positions, although the number and locations of available positions may change according to host-organization needs and local or regional circumstances. The fellowships cover a broad range of professional areas, including education, public health, environmental sustainability, economic development, arts and culture, sports, STEM, and peace, justice, and access to information.

Unlike programs that are limited to a particular academic discipline, Princeton in Asia encourages applicants from a wide range of educational and professional backgrounds. The fellowship is particularly relevant for college seniors, recent graduates, and other early-career professionals seeking international work experience and a structured opportunity to live and work in an Asian community.

What Is Princeton in Asia?

Princeton in Asia (PiA) is an organization affiliated with Princeton University that facilitates immersive work fellowships in Asia. Its mission is to foster mutual appreciation and cross-cultural understanding between the United States and Asia through professional placements in host organizations and communities.

PiA describes its work as a form of person-to-person diplomacy, with Fellows expected not only to contribute professionally to their host organizations but also to develop meaningful relationships within the communities where they live and work.

The program has a long history of international engagement. According to PiA, more than 3,400 Fellows and Interns have participated in its programs across more than 30 countries and regions in Asia since its establishment.

The 2027-28 fellowship cycle therefore offers applicants an opportunity to combine professional development, international experience, community engagement, and cross-cultural learning.

Princeton in Asia Fellowship 2027-28 at a Glance

  • Program: Princeton in Asia Fellowship
  • Fellowship cycle: 2027-28
  • Expected positions: Approximately 60
  • Duration: One or two years, depending on the fellowship
  • Expected start period: Generally July to September 2027
  • Application opening date: September 1, 2026
  • Application deadline: November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST
  • Location: Various host organizations and communities across Asia
  • Academic requirement: Bachelor’s degree by the start of the fellowship
  • Nationality: Applicants of any nationality may apply, subject to PiA eligibility and host-country visa requirements
  • English requirement: Professional proficiency in English
  • Age limit: None
  • Application fee: None

PiA’s official application timeline confirms that applications opened on September 1, 2026, and that all application materials must be submitted online by November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time.

Where Can Princeton in Asia Fellows Be Placed?

The 2027-28 fellowship cycle is expected to include placements across multiple Asian countries and regions. The opportunities described for the cycle include:

  • Cambodia
  • China
  • Hong Kong SAR
  • Indonesia
  • Japan
  • Kazakhstan
  • Kyrgyzstan
  • Laos
  • Macao SAR
  • Mongolia
  • Singapore
  • Sri Lanka
  • Taiwan
  • Thailand
  • Uzbekistan
  • Vietnam

Applicants should understand that the precise list of positions and locations can change. PiA works with host organizations to determine their staffing needs, and host-country circumstances, visa requirements, and organizational needs can affect the final availability of posts.

The organization also explains that applicants will be able to indicate placement preferences during the 2027-28 application process. These preferences help PiA understand an applicant’s interests but do not function as an absolute restriction on placement. Applicants are encouraged to remain open to opportunities outside their initial preferences.

What Areas Do Princeton in Asia Fellowships Cover?

One of the defining features of the PiA program is the diversity of professional fields represented by its fellowships.

The program includes opportunities in:

1. Arts and Culture

Applicants interested in cultural institutions, creative industries, heritage, arts programming, and related fields may find positions connected to this area.

2. Economic Development

Some fellowships involve economic development, business-related activities, entrepreneurship, or work supporting economic growth and development initiatives.

3. Education

Education is an important component of PiA’s fellowship portfolio. Positions may involve teaching, educational administration, curriculum-related activities, university work, or other education-focused responsibilities.

Teaching positions have an additional English-language requirement, and candidates placed in teaching roles complete PiA’s teacher-training program.

4. Environmental Sustainability

Applicants interested in environmental issues, sustainability, conservation, climate-related work, or sustainable development may find relevant opportunities among the available placements.

5. Peace, Justice, and Access to Information

PiA also supports placements involving areas such as peacebuilding, justice, information access, and related social-impact work.

6. Public Health

Public health is another fellowship focus area, creating opportunities for applicants interested in health systems, community health, health education, and related fields.

7. Sports

The fellowship portfolio can also include positions connected to sports and community engagement through sporting activities.

8. Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics

STEM-related fellowships can involve scientific, technological, engineering, mathematical, educational, research, or related professional activities.

PiA confirms that it is not exclusively an English-teaching program. Its fellowship portfolio spans arts and culture, economic development, education, environmental sustainability, public health, sports, STEM, and peace, justice, and access to information.

What Does the Princeton in Asia Fellowship Offer?

The fellowship provides Fellows with a combination of professional placement, financial support, preparation, health and safety resources, and access to a broader international alumni community.

Paid Work Experience in Asia

PiA Fellows undertake immersive work placements with host organizations in Asia. These are professional roles rather than simply cultural exchange visits.

The work allows Fellows to contribute their skills to a host organization while developing practical experience in an international environment.

Living Stipend

Fellows receive a local living stipend from the host organization.

PiA explains that the stipend is intended to support basic living costs associated with the fellowship, including:

  • Housing, where housing is not directly provided by the host organization
  • Food and groceries
  • Local transportation
  • Telecommunications

PiA also clarifies that the stipend is designed for basic living expenses and is not intended to function as a source of substantial personal income or to finance extensive leisure travel.

Health and Safety Support

Fellows receive health, safety, and welfare support. PiA’s current program information states that Fellows receive travel medical and emergency evacuation insurance, International SOS membership, mental-health support, and pre-departure preparation and resources.

This support is particularly relevant for applicants who may be living and working abroad for the first time.

Pre-Departure Orientation

Selected Fellows participate in preparation before departing for their host country.

The 2027-28 timeline indicates that all Fellows will attend a mandatory multi-day orientation in Princeton, New Jersey in early June 2027.

This preparation is intended to help Fellows understand the practical, professional, and cultural dimensions of their upcoming placements.

TEFL Training for Teaching Fellows

Applicants do not need previous TEFL certification or teaching experience to apply to PiA.

However, candidates who receive a teaching placement will be required to complete PiA’s teacher-training course. For the 2027-28 cycle, Teaching Fellows are expected to complete a 120-hour Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL) online certification course before beginning their fellowship.

Visa and Work Permit Support

Fellows work with host organizations during the visa and work-permit process.

PiA’s current information indicates that visa and work-permit costs before departure are supported, including reimbursement for applicable U.S.-side visa expenses. Fellows must still obtain the appropriate authorization and meet the immigration requirements applicable to their placement.

Travel Support

Applicants should distinguish the fellowship’s living support from international travel costs.

PiA states that Fellows are generally responsible for round-trip airfare to their host community. However, the organization provides travel grants intended to reduce this financial burden, and some host organizations cover airfare.

Country Advisors

PiA provides Fellows with access to Country Advisors who have significant experience and local knowledge of the countries where PiA operates.

These advisors can help Fellows better understand local culture, norms, behavior, and other aspects of adapting to life and work in the host community.

Alumni Network

Fellows also become part of the Princeton in Asia alumni community.

PiA provides access to its Alumni Network and mentor directory, giving participants an opportunity to remain connected to former Fellows and the wider PiA community after completing their placements.

Language Grants

PiA also identifies language grants as an available form of support, subject to application. Asian language skills themselves are not generally required for most positions, although individual fellowship descriptions may specify particular language requirements.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The primary academic requirement is a bachelor’s degree.

Applicants must have completed their bachelor’s degree before the beginning of their fellowship. Candidates with master’s degrees may also apply.

However, PiA does not accept candidates whose highest degree is a professional or terminal degree such as:

  • Ph.D.
  • M.D.
  • J.D.

Graduates of any college or university can apply. Applicants do not need to be Princeton University graduates or students.

PiA also does not impose an age limit. Although many Fellows are college seniors or recent graduates, individuals who graduated several years ago can still apply.

Can International Applicants Apply?

Yes.

Princeton in Asia states that applicants of any nationality may apply. However, citizenship alone does not determine eligibility for placement.

Applicants who are not U.S. citizens generally need to demonstrate a meaningful connection to the United States that enables them to contribute to PiA’s mission of U.S.-Asia exchange. PiA states that this generally means having either:

  • Attended a U.S.-accredited institution; or
  • Lived in the United States for one year or more.

Applicants should also understand that host-country immigration and visa regulations can affect whether a person of a particular nationality can be placed in a particular fellowship.

Therefore, being from an Asian, African, European, American, or other country does not by itself create a blanket exclusion from applying. The applicant must satisfy PiA’s broader eligibility requirements and be legally placeable in the relevant host country.

English-Language Requirements

Professional proficiency in English is required for all PiA positions.

For English-teaching positions, the requirement is higher: applicants must have native or near-native English-speaking ability.

Knowledge of an Asian language can be useful and may be specifically requested for certain placements, but Asian language skills are not required for most PiA fellowships. Applicants should therefore carefully examine the requirements of individual fellowship positions when deciding where their skills may fit.

Does an Applicant Need Previous Experience in Asia?

Not necessarily.

PiA explains that previous experience in Asia is not generally required for most positions. Some specific fellowships may require knowledge of or professional experience in Asia, including Asian-language skills, but many placements are designed for applicants who are interested in learning about Asia through an immersive experience.

PiA’s selection process places emphasis on qualities such as adaptability, resilience, resourcefulness, professionalism, self-management, commitment, and the ability to build relationships across cultures.

What Kind of Applicants Is PiA Looking For?

Academic qualifications are only one part of the application.

PiA states that it seeks candidates who can contribute to its mission of fostering mutual appreciation and cross-cultural understanding between the United States and Asia.

The organization identifies several qualities associated with its Fellows, including:

  • Openness to personal transformation
  • Willingness to become immersed in the host community
  • Ability to build meaningful relationships
  • Humility and respect for different perspectives
  • Commitment to mutual learning
  • Desire to contribute to the host organization and community
  • Strong work ethic
  • Resourcefulness
  • Self-management
  • Adaptability
  • Resilience
  • Professional readiness

Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain not only what they can do professionally but also why they are interested in an immersive cross-cultural experience and how they can contribute to the community in which they will live and work.

How Long Does the Fellowship Last?

PiA fellowships typically last one or two years.

Most positions are structured as one-year fellowships, although some positions are specifically designed as two-year placements. PiA also encourages first-year Fellows to consider staying for a second year where the particular fellowship permits it.

According to the official 2027-28 timeline, most fellowships are expected to begin in August 2027, although some may begin in July or September depending on host-organization needs. All placements are contingent upon obtaining the required visa and completing PiA’s pre-departure requirements.

Princeton in Asia 2027-28 Application Timeline

Applicants should pay close attention to the following dates:

September 1, 2026

The 2027-28 fellowship application opens.

November 1, 2026

All application materials must be submitted online by 11:59 PM EST.

December 21, 2026

Applicants are expected to be notified about whether they have been selected for interviews with PiA staff.

January 2027

Virtual interviews with PiA staff are scheduled.

Late February 2027

Applicants are expected to receive notification of nominee status or an invitation to join the waitlist.

Late February to March 2027

Nominees submit additional materials for review by potential host organizations.

March to April 2027

Host organizations evaluate nominees and communicate their selections to PiA.

Late March onward

PiA begins extending fellowship offers on a rolling basis until positions are filled.

April to August 2027

Selected Fellows begin the visa and work-permit process with their host organizations.

April to May 2027

Teaching Fellows complete the required 120-hour TEFL online certification course.

Early June 2027

All Fellows attend a mandatory multi-day orientation in Princeton, New Jersey.

July to September 2027

Most fellowships begin, with the majority expected to start in August.

Click HERE to register for an information session.

Application Deadline

The Princeton in Asia 2027-28 Fellowship application deadline is November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their materials because the application requires several components and late submissions may not be accepted.

APPLY HERE

What Is Required for the Application?

The PiA application includes several components designed to help the organization understand an applicant’s academic background, professional preparation, communication abilities, motivations, and suitability for the fellowship.

The application includes:

  1. Online application form
  2. Two written responses
  3. One 60-second video
  4. Resume
  5. Unofficial college or university transcript
  6. Demographic survey
  7. One recommendation form completed by a selected recommender

Applicants should therefore begin preparing their materials well before the November deadline.

A strong application should provide a coherent explanation of the applicant’s academic and professional background, relevant skills, interest in the fellowship, and ability to contribute to PiA’s cross-cultural mission.

Important Application Guidance

Applicants should pay close attention to PiA’s application and placement process.

PiA advises applicants not to contact host organizations directly during the application process. Host organizations are introduced to applicants through PiA at the appropriate stage. According to PiA, applicants who circumvent the official selection process by contacting host organizations directly can be automatically disqualified from consideration.

Applicants should also understand that indicating a preferred country, issue area, or fellowship does not guarantee placement in that particular position. PiA uses applicants’ preferences as guidance while considering the needs and requirements of host organizations.

Maintaining flexibility about location and type of work can therefore be important during the placement process.

Is There an Application Fee?

No.

Princeton in Asia states that there is no fee to apply for its fellowship program.

Is the Princeton in Asia Fellowship Fully Funded?

The PiA fellowship provides substantial support, but applicants should understand what the program does and does not cover.

The fellowship includes a host-provided living stipend intended to cover basic local living costs, as well as health and safety support and assistance with visa and work-permit expenses. PiA also provides travel grants to help reduce international travel costs, while some host organizations may cover airfare.

However, applicants should not automatically interpret the fellowship as a conventional fully funded scholarship that pays every possible expense. PiA specifically notes that Fellows are generally responsible for round-trip airfare, although travel grants and host-organizational support may reduce or cover those costs in some cases. Fellows are also responsible for pre-departure vaccinations and related costs.

How the Selection and Placement Process Works

The PiA selection process takes place over several stages.

First, applicants submit their applications by the November deadline. PiA then reviews applications and invites selected candidates to virtual interviews.

The organization emphasizes that receiving an interview does not guarantee a fellowship position. Following the interview stage, successful candidates can proceed to the nomination stage, where their materials may be considered by specific host organizations.

Host organizations then evaluate nominees according to their own fellowship requirements and communicate their decisions to PiA.

Fellowship offers are subsequently made on a rolling basis beginning in late March 2027 until available positions are filled. Candidates receiving an offer must accept or decline within four calendar days. PiA states that accepting an offer is binding and requires the applicant to withdraw from consideration for other fellowship and job opportunities.

Why the Fellowship Is Different From a Conventional Study-Abroad Program

The Princeton in Asia Fellowship is primarily a work-based international fellowship.

Rather than simply attending classes abroad, Fellows are placed with organizations where they undertake professional responsibilities while living within the host community.

This distinction means applicants should approach the program as both a professional opportunity and a cross-cultural experience.

The fellowship can expose participants to:

  • International workplace environments
  • Cross-cultural communication
  • Community engagement
  • Professional responsibilities in an Asian setting
  • New approaches to education, development, health, sustainability, technology, or other fields
  • International networks
  • Cultural learning
  • Independent living and professional adaptation

The program’s emphasis on immersion means that successful participation involves more than completing assigned workplace duties. PiA describes its Fellows as people who build relationships, learn from their communities, and contribute to mutual understanding between the United States and Asia.

APPLY HERE

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants can begin preparing well before the deadline by taking several practical steps.

1. Start With the Eligibility Requirements

Confirm that you will have the required bachelor’s degree before the fellowship begins and review the rules concerning citizenship, U.S. education or residency, English proficiency, and host-country visa requirements.

2. Research the Fellowship Areas

Think carefully about the areas in which your academic background, professional experience, skills, and interests could contribute.

PiA’s fellowship areas extend well beyond English teaching, so applicants should consider education, public health, sustainability, economic development, STEM, arts and culture, sports, and peace and justice-related opportunities.

3. Prepare Your Resume Early

Your resume should clearly communicate your education, professional experience, leadership activities, community engagement, technical skills, language abilities, and other experiences relevant to the fellowship.

4. Prepare the Written Responses Carefully

The written responses provide an opportunity to explain your motivations and demonstrate how your experiences connect to PiA’s mission.

Applicants should avoid simply repeating information already listed on their resume. Instead, the responses should demonstrate reflection, purpose, adaptability, and an understanding of why an immersive international fellowship fits their goals.

5. Plan the 60-Second Video

The application includes a short video, meaning applicants need to communicate effectively within a very limited amount of time.

A concise and authentic presentation can help communicate personality, motivation, communication ability, and interest in cross-cultural engagement.

6. Choose Your Recommender Carefully

The recommendation form is another component of the application. Applicants should select someone who knows their academic, professional, leadership, or community-related work well enough to provide meaningful evidence of their abilities and character.

7. Consider Geographic Flexibility

PiA asks applicants to identify placement preferences, but those preferences are not necessarily binding. Applicants should remain open to opportunities outside their first-choice country or position.

8. Do Not Contact Host Organizations Independently

All communication with potential host organizations should follow PiA’s official process. Directly circumventing the process can result in disqualification.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Princeton in Asia Fellowship 2027-28.

Official Application and Further Information

Applicants should use Princeton in Asia’s official fellowship application resources for the current 2027-28 cycle.

The official application page provides the application portal, application guide, timeline, fellowship descriptions, and information about the selection process.

Official Princeton in Asia Fellowship Application:
Apply for the Princeton in Asia 2027-28 Fellowship

Applicants can also review PiA’s official eligibility requirements before submitting an application.

Official eligibility information:
Princeton in Asia Fellowship Eligibility

Conclusion

The Princeton in Asia Fellowship 2027-28 offers bachelor’s degree holders an opportunity to undertake immersive professional work in Asia while participating in cross-cultural exchange and community engagement. The program is open to graduates of universities beyond Princeton and has no age limit, while applicants of any nationality can apply subject to PiA’s U.S.-Asia exchange requirement and host-country visa rules.

The fellowship covers a wide range of professional fields, including education, public health, environmental sustainability, economic development, arts and culture, sports, STEM, and peace, justice, and access to information. Fellows receive a local living stipend from their host organization, health and safety support, pre-departure preparation, access to the PiA alumni network, and other forms of assistance.

The application deadline is November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. Applicants interested in the 2027-28 cycle should begin preparing their resume, written responses, video, transcript, recommendation, and other application materials early and should carefully review the specific fellowship descriptions and eligibility requirements before submitting.

Because fellowship positions and host-country opportunities can change, applicants should rely on the official Princeton in Asia application portal for the latest information throughout the application and selection process.

item.content:encoded:
The Rise to Lead: Girl Up 2026 Global Leadership Summit is an upcoming virtual global gathering designed to bring young people and youth leaders together to explore leadership, gender justice, social change, and the future of youth-led movements.

Organized by Girl Up, the virtual summit will take place on October 10, 2026, at 4:00 PM Africa/Addis Ababa time and will provide young people from around the world with an opportunity to hear directly from youth leaders and changemakers, participate in conversations across generations, discover new perspectives on leadership, and connect with a global community of young people working toward gender justice.

The event is particularly relevant for young people who want to understand what leadership can look like in today’s rapidly changing world and how they can contribute to movements that promote gender equality and social change.

Importantly, participants do not have to be current Girl Up leaders or members of a Girl Up Club. The summit is open to young people between the ages of 13 and 24 who are interested in leadership, creating change, or becoming connected with the broader Girl Up community.

About the Rise to Lead Global Leadership Summit

Leadership is changing, particularly within youth-led movements. Young people around the world are increasingly taking active roles in addressing issues affecting their communities, advocating for gender equality, building organizations, developing campaigns, and creating new approaches to social change.

The Rise to Lead summit is designed around this changing understanding of leadership.

Rather than focusing only on traditional ideas of leadership, the event invites participants to consider an important question:

What kind of leadership does the movement for gender justice need right now, and what role can young people play in shaping what comes next?

The summit will create a space for young people to listen, learn, exchange ideas, and connect with others who are interested in gender justice and youth leadership.

Through conversations involving youth voices and different generations, participants will have the opportunity to explore how leadership can be practiced in different ways and how young people can contribute to movements for meaningful change.

What Is Girl Up?

Girl Up is a global movement focused on supporting young people and advancing gender equality. Its community brings together young leaders who are interested in creating change and addressing issues affecting girls and women.

The Rise to Lead Global Leadership Summit is part of Girl Up’s broader leadership and community-building activities and will launch the organization’s 2026 Summit Series.

The virtual event will therefore serve not only as a standalone global gathering but also as the beginning of a wider series of leadership events taking place in different regions around the world.

What Can Participants Expect?

The Rise to Lead summit is planned as a dynamic one-hour virtual event featuring youth voices, conversations across generations, new ideas, and opportunities for global connection.

Participants can expect the program to focus on several interconnected areas.

1. Youth Leadership

Youth leadership is at the center of the summit.

Young people will have the opportunity to hear from other youth leaders and changemakers and explore how young people are contributing to social movements and creating change within their communities.

The event recognizes that young people are not simply future leaders. They are already participating in movements and initiatives that influence communities and conversations around the world.

2. Gender Justice

A major focus of the summit is gender justice.

Participants will explore the role that leadership can play in advancing gender equality and addressing challenges affecting girls and young women.

The summit provides an opportunity for young people interested in gender justice to connect with others who share an interest in creating more equitable communities and systems.

3. Conversations Across Generations

Another important component of the event is the opportunity to engage with perspectives from different generations.

Leadership and social change can benefit from conversations between people with different experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives.

The summit will bring youth voices together with broader leadership perspectives to encourage discussion about what effective leadership looks like today and how movements can continue to evolve.

4. New Ideas and Perspectives

Participants will also have the opportunity to discover new ideas surrounding leadership and social change.

The summit is intended to encourage young people to think about leadership beyond conventional definitions and consider different ways they can contribute to their communities and movements.

5. Global Connection

Because the summit is virtual and designed as a global event, participants can connect with young people from different parts of the world.

This creates an opportunity to learn about different experiences, perspectives, challenges, and approaches to gender justice and youth leadership.

For young people interested in international communities and youth movements, the global nature of the event can be an important part of the experience.

Who Can Participate in the Girl Up 2026 Summit?

The event is specifically designed for young people aged 13 to 24.

One of the important features of the opportunity is that participants do not need to have an existing connection with Girl Up.

You can participate even if you:

  • Are not currently a Girl Up Club member
  • Have never participated in a Girl Up program
  • Are not currently a youth leader
  • Are interested in developing your leadership skills
  • Want to learn more about gender justice
  • Are interested in creating positive change
  • Want to connect with other young people globally
  • Are considering becoming part of the Girl Up community

The announcement specifically states that young people who are interested in leadership, creating change, or becoming part of the Girl Up community are welcome to participate.

Is the Summit Open to Young People Outside the United States?

Yes. The event is presented as a global virtual leadership summit, with young people from around the world invited to participate.

The announcement does not identify a specific country or continental restriction. It also does not state any race or ethnicity restriction.

Because the summit is virtual, eligible participants can join from their respective countries as long as they meet the stated age requirement and can participate in the online event.

This makes the summit potentially accessible to young people across Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions around the world.

Young people in countries such as Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania, India, the Philippines, Vietnam, Mexico, the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and other countries can consider registering, provided they meet the event requirements.

However, because the provided announcement does not provide a formal country-by-country eligibility list, applicants should rely on the official registration information for any additional participation requirements.

Do You Need to Be a Girl Up Member?

No.

This is an important point for prospective participants.

The summit is not restricted to current Girl Up leaders or Girl Up Club members.

If you have never participated in Girl Up activities before but are interested in leadership, gender justice, youth movements, or creating change, you can still participate.

This makes the summit accessible to young people who may be discovering the Girl Up community for the first time.

Why Attend the Rise to Lead Summit?

The summit offers several potential learning and networking opportunities for young people interested in leadership and social change.

Learn From Youth Leaders

Participants will hear from young leaders and changemakers who are contributing to movements and initiatives focused on social change.

This can help participants gain exposure to different leadership experiences and approaches.

Explore New Ideas About Leadership

The event encourages participants to think about leadership in the context of today’s challenges.

Rather than presenting leadership as a single model, the summit creates space for young people to consider what leadership can mean within movements for gender justice.

Connect With a Global Youth Community

Participants can connect virtually with young people who share interests in leadership, gender equality, advocacy, and social change.

These connections can expose participants to perspectives and experiences from different communities and countries.

Discover the Girl Up Community

For young people who are not currently involved with Girl Up, the summit can provide an introduction to the organization’s broader community and leadership activities.

Participants who are interested in becoming more involved can use the event as an opportunity to learn more about the movement.

Gain Exposure to Gender Justice Conversations

Young people interested in gender equality can gain exposure to discussions surrounding leadership and gender justice while engaging with other participants who are interested in creating change.

Girl Up’s 2026 Summit Series

The Rise to Lead virtual summit is also significant because it marks the beginning of Girl Up’s 2026 Summit Series.

Following the virtual global event, Girl Up plans to continue the summit experience through in-person regional Summits in different parts of the world.

The announcement specifically highlights upcoming regional summit activities connected with:

  • Vietnam
  • Kenya
  • México

This means that Rise to Lead is positioned as the opening event for a broader 2026 summit experience rather than an isolated online meeting.

Young people who participate in the virtual summit can therefore become familiar with the wider leadership community and future regional activities.

Event Details

Event Details
Event Name Rise to Lead: Girl Up 2026 Global Leadership Summit
Organizer Girl Up
Format Virtual
Date October 10, 2026
Time 4:00 PM Africa/Addis Ababa
Duration Approximately one hour
Age Eligibility 13–24
Membership Requirement No current Girl Up membership required
Geographic Scope Global
Main Focus Youth leadership and gender justice
Registration Required to save a spot
Application Deadline Not specified in the provided announcement

What Will the Summit Focus On?

The central theme of the event revolves around the future of leadership within the gender justice movement.

The summit asks participants to consider what leadership is needed at this point in time and what role each young person can play in shaping future movements.

The discussion therefore connects several themes:

  1. Youth leadership
  2. Gender justice
  3. Social change
  4. Intergenerational dialogue
  5. Global youth connection
  6. Community building
  7. Leadership development
  8. New approaches to creating change

These themes make the summit relevant to young people who are already involved in advocacy as well as those who are only beginning to explore leadership and social-impact activities.

Registration Information

Interested young people are encouraged to register in advance to save their spot at the virtual summit.

The provided announcement does not give a specific registration closing date. Therefore, prospective participants should register as early as possible rather than waiting until the event date.

The summit is scheduled for:

October 10, 2026
4:00 PM Africa/Addis Ababa time

Participants should also check their local time zone if they are joining from outside Ethiopia or another location that uses the Africa/Addis Ababa time zone.

Is There an Application Fee?

The announcement provided does not mention an application fee or participation fee.

Prospective participants should consult the official registration page for the most current information about registration requirements, participation arrangements, and any conditions associated with attending the virtual event.

Important Deadline Information

No specific registration deadline is stated in the opportunity information provided.

However, because the event is scheduled for October 10, 2026, interested young people should complete registration before the event.

The key date to remember is:

Event Date: October 10, 2026

Event Time: 4:00 PM Africa/Addis Ababa

Who Should Consider Registering?

The summit may be particularly relevant to young people aged 13–24 who are:

  • Interested in youth leadership
  • Interested in gender equality and gender justice
  • Involved in community initiatives
  • Interested in social change
  • Youth advocates or emerging activists
  • Interested in developing leadership experience
  • Interested in international youth communities
  • Interested in connecting with changemakers
  • Looking for opportunities to learn from other young leaders
  • Interested in becoming part of the Girl Up community
  • Curious about how young people can contribute to gender justice movements

You do not need to already consider yourself an established leader. The event is also intended for young people who are interested in leadership and want to explore how they can contribute to positive change.

Global Accessibility of the Opportunity

One of the notable aspects of Rise to Lead is its virtual format and global positioning.

Unlike an event requiring participants to travel to a particular country, the virtual summit allows eligible young people to participate online from different parts of the world.

The announcement does not restrict participation to a particular continent or nationality. It also does not specify any race or ethnicity requirement.

The primary eligibility condition explicitly identified is age 13–24, alongside an interest in leadership, creating change, or becoming part of the Girl Up community.

Participants should nevertheless review the official registration terms before registering in case additional technical or participation requirements are provided on the registration platform.

How This Opportunity Fits Into Girl Up’s Broader Activities

Rise to Lead forms part of a broader leadership and summit program planned by Girl Up for 2026.

The virtual summit provides a global starting point, while regional in-person events are expected to continue the experience.

The announcement identifies Vietnam, Kenya, and México as locations associated with the 2026 Summit Series.

This structure provides different opportunities for young people to engage with the Girl Up community: first through a global virtual gathering and subsequently through regional experiences.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The Rise to Lead: Girl Up 2026 Global Leadership Summit provides an opportunity for young people aged 13–24 to participate in a global conversation about youth leadership, gender justice, and creating change.

The virtual format makes the event accessible to young people from different parts of the world, while the absence of a requirement to be an existing Girl Up leader or Club member means that young people who are new to the Girl Up community can also participate.

Through youth voices, intergenerational conversations, new ideas, and opportunities for global connection, the summit is designed to encourage participants to think about the role they can play in shaping future movements for gender justice.

The event will take place on October 10, 2026, at 4:00 PM Africa/Addis Ababa time. Although the provided announcement does not specify a registration deadline, interested young people should register ahead of the event to save their spot.

For young people between 13 and 24 who are interested in leadership, social change, gender justice, or joining a global youth community, Rise to Lead offers an opportunity to learn, connect, and explore different ways of contributing to movements for change.
