item.content:encoded:
The 2027 Bush Fellowship is now accepting applications from leaders who are ready to invest in their own leadership development and build the capacity needed to create meaningful, equitable and large-scale change.

Offered by the Bush Foundation, the Bush Fellowship is a self-designed leadership development opportunity that gives selected Fellows the time and financial resources to pursue a personalized plan for becoming a stronger and more effective leader.

For the 2027 cohort, up to 30 Bush Fellows will be selected, with each Fellow eligible to receive up to $150,000 to support their individual Fellowship plan over a period of up to two years. The program welcomes leaders from different sectors, including business, government and nonprofit organizations.

The application deadline is October 6, 2026, at noon Central Time (CT). Applications opened on September 22, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. CT.

What Is the Bush Fellowship?

The Bush Fellowship is designed for individuals who have already demonstrated leadership and impact and who understand that they need to invest in their own development to increase their ability to create change.

Rather than providing conventional funding for an organization, business or specific community project, the Fellowship focuses on the individual leader.

The program gives Fellows the flexibility to design their own leadership development plans according to their goals, circumstances and vision for the change they want to make.

According to the Bush Foundation, Bush Fellows are individuals who make things happen and who are often responsible for making change possible. They are people who have reached a point in their leadership journey where they understand what they need to grow and have a plan for how they intend to do it.

This makes the Bush Fellowship particularly relevant to established leaders who are looking beyond conventional professional development and want to make a significant transformation in how they lead.

Key Highlights of the 2027 Bush Fellowship

The opportunity offers several significant benefits for successful applicants:

  • Up to $150,000 in Fellowship support
  • Up to two years to implement a self-designed leadership development plan
  • Selection of up to 30 Bush Fellows each year
  • Flexibility to design an individualized leadership development experience
  • Opportunity to invest substantial time and resources into leadership growth
  • Open to leaders working across multiple sectors, including business, government and nonprofit organizations
  • A structured selection process involving application review, references, background checks and interviews
  • Participation in a Bush Fellowship retreat for selected Fellows
  • Connection to a wider community of Bush Fellows and leaders
  • Opportunity to pursue ambitious personal development activities that can strengthen a Fellow’s ability to create broader change

The Bush Foundation has invested in more than 2,000 Fellows since the Fellowship began in the 1960s, demonstrating the longstanding nature of the program.

What Does the Bush Fellowship Fund?

The Bush Fellowship is intentionally different from a traditional project grant.

The Foundation is looking for individuals who want to invest in their own leadership capacity, rather than applicants seeking money to create, expand or complete a project.

The Fellowship can support a range of activities that contribute to an individual’s leadership development, provided they are connected to a strong and clearly articulated Fellowship plan.

The Bush Foundation encourages applicants to think broadly about what they need to become a more effective leader.

For example, a Fellowship plan could involve:

  1. Advanced learning and professional development

    A Fellow may use the opportunity to participate in an educational or professional development program that builds capabilities needed to address complex problems.

  2. Learning from other countries or communities

    A Fellow working in an area such as language revitalization could, for example, travel internationally to learn from another movement or community that has developed relevant approaches.

  3. Taking time away from an existing role

    A Fellow with an ambitious vision for change may use the Fellowship to reduce their work commitments or temporarily step away from their current position to dedicate substantial time to developing and implementing their leadership vision.

  4. Developing new approaches to leadership

    Applicants are encouraged to think beyond conventional training and consider what experiences, resources, relationships, learning opportunities or periods of focused reflection could significantly change the trajectory of their leadership journey.

The Foundation emphasizes that there is no single formula for designing a Fellowship plan. The plan should reflect the individual’s circumstances, leadership goals and vision for change.

Who Is the Bush Foundation Looking For?

The Bush Foundation identifies three major qualities it seeks in Bush Fellowship applicants.

1. Leaders With a Track Record of Impact

The Foundation is looking for people who have already demonstrated that they can create meaningful results.

Bush Fellows are described as problem solvers who get things done. They demonstrate strong character and an openness to learning from other people.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate more than ambition. Their application should communicate evidence of what they have accomplished and the difference their leadership has already made.

2. Leaders With a Vision for Change

The Fellowship is also intended for people who have a significant vision for the future.

Applicants should be able to articulate the change they want to make happen and explain how they are uniquely positioned to contribute to that change.

The Foundation specifically emphasizes a vision for equitable, large-scale change.

This means applicants should think carefully about the relationship between their personal leadership development and the broader change they hope to contribute to.

3. Leaders With a Clear Development Plan

A strong vision alone is not enough.

Applicants need a clear plan explaining how they would use the time and resources provided through the Fellowship to develop their leadership capacity.

The Fellowship plan is described by the Foundation as the foundation of the Fellowship itself.

Applicants should therefore be able to explain:

  • What they need to learn or develop
  • Why that development is important at this stage of their leadership journey
  • How they intend to use the Fellowship resources
  • What experiences or opportunities would help them grow
  • How the proposed development connects to their broader vision for change
  • Why the Fellowship is particularly relevant to their current circumstances

The Foundation notes that if an applicant does not have a clear plan for investing in their own leadership development, another Fellowship or leadership resource may be a better fit.

The Bush Fellowship Is About Investing in the Leader

One of the most important aspects of the Bush Fellowship is its focus on personal leadership development.

Applicants may naturally be inclined to focus on how their Fellowship would benefit their organization, community or cause. However, the Bush Foundation encourages applicants to think about the investment in themselves as a mechanism for creating broader impact.

The Foundation acknowledges that some leaders find it difficult to think about investing resources in themselves rather than directly investing in their communities.

However, the program’s approach is based on the idea that strengthening a leader’s capacity can ultimately strengthen the leader’s ability to contribute to their community and create change.

Examples of Bush Fellowship Plans

The Foundation provides several examples to help potential applicants understand the type of leadership development plan that may fit the program.

One example involves a leader who wants to strengthen their understanding of public policy advocacy and develop new skills for solving complex problems. Such an applicant could use the Fellowship to participate in a relevant policy fellowship or learning program.

Another example involves someone working on language revitalization who wants to travel to New Zealand to learn from efforts to revitalize the Māori language.

A further example involves a leader with an ambitious vision who may need significant time away from their current responsibilities to develop themselves and activate their vision for change.

These examples demonstrate the flexibility of the Bush Fellowship and the importance of connecting the proposed activities to a broader leadership-development objective.

Who Can Benefit From the Bush Fellowship?

The Fellowship welcomes leaders working across different sectors.

The Foundation specifically identifies:

  • Business leaders
  • Government leaders
  • Nonprofit leaders
  • Individuals who have demonstrated leadership and impact
  • Leaders with a vision for equitable and large-scale change
  • Individuals who understand what they need to develop in order to become more effective leaders
  • People who can develop a clear and realistic plan for using the Fellowship resources

The Foundation also notes that people do not necessarily have to think of themselves as traditional “leaders.” Its definition is broader: if someone is the person who makes things happen and their contribution is essential to achieving change, they may already be exercising leadership.

Who Is the Fellowship Not Designed For?

Understanding what the Fellowship does not fund is just as important as understanding what it does fund.

The Bush Fellowship is not intended for individuals who simply want to:

  • Create a project
  • Expand an existing project
  • Complete a project
  • Fund a business

Applicants whose primary objective is to secure funding for one of these purposes may need to explore other Bush Foundation programs, fellowships or leadership-development resources.

The Foundation provides information about other programs for people seeking different forms of support.

Important Restrictions on How Fellowship Funds Can Be Used

Although the Bush Fellowship provides considerable flexibility, the funding comes with specific restrictions.

Among the limitations identified by the Foundation are:

  • Fellowship funds cannot be directed to another person or organization.
  • Funds cannot be used to fund a business.
  • Funds cannot be used to fund a program.
  • Funds cannot be used to pay off debt.
  • Funds cannot be used for lobbying.
  • Funds cannot be used for political contributions.
  • Funds cannot be used for expenses related to political campaigns.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed Fellowship plan is genuinely focused on their own leadership development and complies with the Foundation’s funding rules.

Additional Rules for Government and Elected Officials

There are additional restrictions for government officials and elected officials because of applicable IRS regulations.

The Foundation states that government and elected officials may only use a Fellowship in a degree-granting program.

The Foundation also provides definitions of the categories of government officials covered by these restrictions.

Federal Government Officials

The Foundation’s definition includes individuals who:

  • Hold elective office in the executive or legislative branch
  • Are presidentially appointed to an office in the executive or judicial branch
  • Hold specified positions in the executive, legislative or judicial branches of the federal government
  • Hold qualifying positions with compensation at or above the stated threshold
  • Work in the U.S. House or Senate with annual compensation of $15,000 or more
  • Serve as personal or executive assistants or secretaries to qualifying officials

The detailed federal definitions are provided by the Foundation in its Fellowship information.

Tribal, State and Local Government Officials

The Foundation also defines qualifying tribal, state and local employees and officials to include individuals who hold elective or appointive public office in the executive, legislative or judicial branch with independent policymaking ability and annual compensation of $20,000 or more.

Personal or executive assistants and secretaries to qualifying officials are also included in the Foundation’s definition.

Government and elected officials considering the Fellowship should therefore carefully review the specific restrictions before preparing their plans.

2027 Bush Fellowship Application Deadline

The application period for the 2027 Bush Fellowship opened on:

September 22, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. CT

The application deadline is:

October 6, 2026, at noon CT

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their submissions because the Foundation encourages candidates to thoroughly review the application materials, criteria and application questions before applying.

2027 Bush Fellowship Selection Timeline

The Bush Foundation has published a multi-stage selection process for the 2027 Fellowship.

Application Period

September 22, 2026: Applications opened at 8:00 a.m. CT.

October 6, 2026: Applications close at noon CT.

Semifinalist Stage

December 1–4, 2026: Semifinalists will be notified.

Finalist Stage

March 10–15, 2027: Finalists will be notified.

Finalist Interviews

Finalist interviews are scheduled for:

  • April 15, 2027
  • April 19, 2027
  • April 22, 2027

Fellowship Retreat

Selected Fellows must attend the Bush Fellowship retreat from

May 19–21, 2027

Public Announcement

The 2027 Bush Fellows are expected to be publicly announced in June 2027.

How Does the Bush Fellowship Selection Process Work?

The Bush Foundation uses a multi-stage selection process involving Bush staff and board members, previous Bush Fellows and community leaders.

The selection process considers:

  1. Application responses
  2. References from semifinalists
  3. In-person interviews with finalists

According to the Foundation, Bush Fellow alumni initially review applications and select approximately 90 semifinalists.

Bush staff members then conduct reference and background checks for finalists. If information arises during a background check, the Foundation states that it will contact the applicant to understand the situation.

Finalists subsequently participate in interviews with panels of community reviewers who are leaders from across the region.

Community reviewers select the next class of Bush Fellows.

The selected Fellows then come together for a celebration and kickoff retreat before the new class is publicly announced.

How Competitive Is the Bush Fellowship?

The Bush Fellowship is a highly competitive leadership opportunity.

The Foundation states that it received almost 1,200 applications for the 2026 Bush Fellowship, while only up to 30 Fellows are selected each year.

The competitiveness of the Fellowship means applicants should devote considerable attention to communicating their leadership journey, impact, vision and development plan.

However, the Foundation also emphasizes that the application process itself can be valuable. Applicants have reportedly found the process useful for reflecting on their leadership journeys and identifying what they need to create meaningful change.

How to Prepare a Strong Bush Fellowship Application

The Bush Foundation encourages applicants to thoroughly review the application materials, criteria and questions before submitting their applications.

A strong preparation process should include the following.

1. Understand Your Leadership Journey

Before writing the application, reflect on your leadership experience.

Consider:

  • What have you accomplished?
  • What problems have you helped solve?
  • What changes would not have happened without your contribution?
  • What leadership experiences have shaped you?
  • What have you learned from your successes and challenges?

The Foundation wants applicants to communicate their unique perspectives, context and experiences.

2. Identify the Change You Want to Create

Applicants should have a clear vision of the change they want to make happen.

Think beyond immediate projects and consider the larger issue you are trying to address.

Your application should make it possible to understand:

  • The change you want to see
  • Why that change matters
  • The role you want to play
  • Why your leadership development is important to achieving that change

3. Identify Your Development Needs

The Fellowship is an investment in the individual.

Therefore, applicants should identify areas where they need to grow.

These could include new knowledge, leadership capabilities, networks, experiences, exposure to other approaches, professional development or dedicated time for reflection and strategic development.

4. Build a Clear Fellowship Plan

Your Fellowship plan should explain how you intend to use the available resources.

The Foundation emphasizes that the plan is central to the Fellowship.

Applicants should therefore avoid creating a generic professional-development list and instead develop a coherent plan that connects their development needs with their broader leadership vision.

5. Demonstrate Your Track Record of Impact

Applicants should provide evidence that they have already made a difference.

Rather than simply stating that you are passionate about an issue, explain what you have done and what resulted from your actions.

Specific examples can help demonstrate leadership, problem-solving ability and impact.

6. Make Your Writing Clear and Authentic

The Foundation advises applicants to make their written applications as clear as possible.

The application does not need to be perfect or completely error-free, but it needs to clearly communicate what the applicant is trying to accomplish and demonstrate how the proposal meets the Fellowship criteria.

The Foundation also encourages applicants to have other people review their applications.

Can Applicants Use Artificial Intelligence to Prepare Their Application?

The Bush Foundation explicitly addresses the use of artificial intelligence in the application process.

Applicants are allowed to use AI tools to assist with their applications, but the Foundation states that applicants cannot use AI to generate their ideas or plans or to write the application for them.

Instead, the Foundation suggests that AI can be useful for activities such as simplifying writing and removing jargon.

The applicant should remain the main writer and editor, and the final application should still sound like the applicant.

This means applicants should ensure that their Fellowship vision, experiences and development plan genuinely originate from their own leadership journey.

What Happens After Selection?

Successful Fellows are required to participate in the Bush Fellowship retreat scheduled for May 19–21, 2027.

The 2027 Fellows will subsequently be publicly announced in June 2027.

The Fellowship can last for up to two years, giving selected leaders substantial time to pursue their individualized leadership-development plans.

Additional Leadership Resources

The Bush Foundation recognizes that the Bush Fellowship is not the right opportunity for every leader.

For people who need other forms of leadership development, the Foundation provides information about partner-operated programs and Bush-supported programs for individuals.

The Foundation also provides leadership resources for people who may be interested in taking courses, developing specific skills, undertaking a sabbatical or taking dedicated time for health and wellness.

These resources can be useful even for people who ultimately decide not to apply for the Bush Fellowship.

Bush Fellowship Webinars and Application Resources

The Foundation provides several resources to help applicants understand the program.

These include:

  • A recorded 2027 Bush Fellowship question-and-answer session
  • An overview of the Bush Fellowship program
  • A guide to developing a Bush Fellowship plan
  • Information about the selection criteria
  • A leadership reflection guide
  • Information about previous Bush Fellows
  • Access to the Bush Foundation grants database

The leadership reflection guide is designed to help people explore their leadership journeys and think about the impact they want to have, whether or not they ultimately apply for the Fellowship.

Bush Fellowship: Opportunity Summary

For quick reference, the major details of the opportunity are:

Opportunity Details
Opportunity name Bush Fellowship
Cohort 2027 Bush Fellowship
Provider Bush Foundation
Funding Up to $150,000
Fellowship duration Up to 2 years
Number selected Up to 30 Bush Fellows
Focus Leadership development
Approach Self-designed leadership plan
Sectors Business, government and nonprofit
Applications opened September 22, 2026
Application deadline October 6, 2026 at noon CT
Semifinalists notified December 1–4, 2026
Finalists notified March 10–15, 2027
Finalist interviews April 15, 19 and 22, 2027
Fellowship retreat May 19–21, 2027
Fellows announced June 2027

The dates and program details above are provided by the Bush Foundation for the 2027 Fellowship.

Who Qualifies for the 2027 Bush Fellowship?

The supplied Bush Foundation information identifies the target applicants as leaders from different sectors, including business, government and nonprofit organizations.

The Foundation is particularly interested in people who:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of impact
  • Are problem solvers who get things done
  • Demonstrate outstanding character
  • Are open to learning from and with others
  • Have a vision for equitable, large-scale change
  • Understand how they are uniquely positioned to contribute to that change
  • Have clear goals for developing their leadership capacity
  • Can create a meaningful Fellowship plan for using the time and resources provided

The Foundation also emphasizes that leadership does not necessarily require holding a formal leadership title. People who consistently make things happen and whose contribution is essential to creating change may see themselves as leaders within the Foundation’s broader understanding of leadership.

Important Things Applicants Should Know Before Applying

Potential applicants should carefully distinguish the Bush Fellowship from a conventional grant.

This opportunity is primarily about investing in an individual’s leadership capacity. It is not designed to provide funding for a business, project or program.

Applicants should also understand that:

  • The Fellowship is highly competitive.
  • A strong leadership track record is important.
  • Applicants need a clear vision for change.
  • Applicants need a clear plan for their own development.
  • Fellowship resources have restrictions.
  • Government and elected officials are subject to additional restrictions.
  • References are part of the semifinalist process.
  • Finalists participate in an in-person interview.
  • Selected Fellows must attend the Fellowship retreat.
  • Applicants are encouraged to make their applications authentic and clearly connected to their own experiences.
  • AI may assist with simplifying writing and removing jargon, but applicants must remain the main authors and editors of their applications.

APPLY HERE

How to Apply for the 2027 Bush Fellowship

Interested applicants should first review the Bush Foundation’s detailed application questions, eligibility requirements and selection criteria.

The Foundation has provided an online application portal for the 2027 Bush Fellowship.

Application deadline: October 6, 2026, at noon CT.

Applicants should prepare their materials well in advance of the deadline and ensure that their proposed Fellowship plan clearly demonstrates their leadership development needs, previous impact and vision for future change.

Visit HERE for more information about the 2027 Bush Fellowship.

Conclusion

The 2027 Bush Fellowship provides an opportunity for established leaders to step back, reflect on their leadership journey and make a substantial investment in their own capacity to create change.

With up to $150,000 available for up to two years, the Fellowship gives selected leaders significant flexibility to design an individualized leadership-development plan. Rather than requiring Fellows to follow a standardized training program, the Bush Foundation encourages them to think deeply about what they need to become more effective leaders and how that development can help them pursue their vision for equitable, large-scale change.

The opportunity is intended for people who already have a record of impact, have a clear vision for the future and understand what they need to develop in order to take their leadership to another level.

With applications closing on October 6, 2026, at noon CT, prospective applicants should carefully review the official eligibility criteria, application questions, funding restrictions and selection process before submitting their applications.

The Bush Fellowship is ultimately centered on a simple principle: investing in leaders can strengthen their ability to make meaningful change happen. For leaders who have a demonstrated record of impact and a well-developed vision for their next stage of growth, the 2027 Fellowship provides a structured opportunity to turn that leadership-development vision into action.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a university student studying data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or another quantitative discipline? Are you interested in using technology and data to address real-world social challenges while exploring a career in financial services technology?

JPMorganChase is inviting eligible students to apply for its Data for Good Hackathon, a two-day social impact technology event organized by the company’s Tech for Social Good team. The event provides participants with an opportunity to work on real-world challenges faced by nonprofit organizations while collaborating with experienced data and artificial intelligence professionals.

Beyond the hackathon experience itself, participation may provide an opportunity to learn more about and potentially be considered for the 2027 Data & AI Program Summer Internship at JPMorganChase.

The opportunity combines practical data and AI experience, teamwork, social impact, professional networking, and exposure to the recruitment process of one of the world’s major financial services companies.

Overview of the JPMorganChase Data for Good Hackathon

The Data for Good Hackathon is a social impact-focused technology event hosted by JPMorganChase Tech for Social Good.

The initiative is designed to use the technical capabilities of JPMorganChase employees to support communities and nonprofit organizations. During the hackathon, participating students will work with other aspiring data and AI professionals and JPMorganChase technologists to analyze real-world datasets and develop insights that can help address challenges faced by nonprofit organizations.

The event is particularly relevant for students who want to understand how data science, analytics, artificial intelligence, and technology can be applied outside purely commercial applications.

Participants will have the opportunity to work collaboratively over two days, analyze large datasets, develop data-driven insights, and present or communicate recommendations relevant to a nonprofit organization.

The experience can also provide exposure to JPMorganChase’s Data & AI career opportunities.

Potential Pathway to the 2027 Data & AI Summer Internship

One of the important aspects of the opportunity is that participation in Data for Good may lead to an opportunity to learn more about and be considered for the 2027 Data & AI Program Summer Internship.

However, participating in the hackathon does not automatically result in an internship offer.

Students interested in the internship will still need to participate in the company’s standard hiring process, which includes additional interview stages.

The Data for Good experience can therefore serve as an opportunity to demonstrate technical ability, teamwork, communication, analytical thinking, and problem-solving in a practical environment.

JPMorganChase also states that its internship classes are filled on a rolling basis, encouraging qualified applicants to submit their applications as early as possible before the relevant postings close.

About the JPMorganChase Data & AI Program

The 2027 Data & AI Program Summer Internship is designed for students interested in applying data, analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to real-world business problems.

As a Summer Analyst in the Data & AI Program, interns can work on projects involving end-to-end data and AI solutions.

The work may include:

  • Developing data and analytics solutions
  • Building artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions
  • Translating business objectives into measurable outcomes
  • Designing data platforms
  • Developing data pipelines
  • Creating production-ready models
  • Building dashboards and data visualizations
  • Supporting data governance
  • Working with privacy and compliance requirements
  • Collaborating with global technology professionals
  • Working in agile teams
  • Developing recommendations based on data and analysis

The program is therefore designed for students who want to combine technical skills with business problem-solving.

What Happens During the Data for Good Hackathon?

The hackathon takes place over two days, Friday and Saturday.

Participants will form teams and work on social-impact data challenges associated with nonprofit organizations.

During the event, participants are expected to use analytical and coding skills to examine large datasets, identify meaningful patterns, develop insights, and contribute to solutions for real-world problems.

The experience involves both technical and collaborative work.

Participants will work alongside JPMorganChase data and AI professionals, giving them an opportunity to observe how experienced technologists approach complex analytical challenges.

The hackathon also provides opportunities to interact with fellow aspiring data and AI professionals from across the United States.

Key Activities and Responsibilities

Participants in the Data for Good experience are expected to demonstrate ownership, collaboration, communication, and analytical problem-solving.

Key expectations include:

1. Own Projects From Start to Finish

Participants will be expected to take responsibility for their team’s work and contribute to the development of projects from initial analysis through to recommendations and outcomes.

This includes keeping team members and stakeholders informed about project progress.

2. Collaborate With Technologists

Participants will work with JPMorganChase technology professionals and other students.

Collaboration is an important part of the experience because data and AI projects typically require people with different technical and professional perspectives to work together.

3. Analyze Large Datasets

A central part of the hackathon involves analyzing large, social-good datasets and using analytical techniques to identify useful information.

Students can apply their knowledge of data science, statistics, programming, machine learning, and quantitative analysis to real-world problems.

4. Develop Data-Driven Recommendations

Participants are expected to transform their analysis into useful recommendations and insights that can help stakeholders understand and address the challenges being examined.

5. Share Ideas and Innovation

The event encourages participants to exchange ideas, approaches, and technical solutions with other participants and JPMorganChase professionals.

6. Work in Agile Teams

The experience provides exposure to collaborative, agile approaches to technology and data projects.

Data & AI Skills That Can Be Relevant

The internship description identifies several technical capabilities that can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Preferred areas include:

  • Data science
  • Machine learning
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Prompt engineering
  • Data analysis
  • Quantitative analysis
  • SQL
  • Python
  • Large and complex datasets
  • Data management
  • Data governance
  • Data platforms
  • Data pipelines
  • Data models
  • Taxonomies
  • Metadata
  • Data lineage
  • Privacy
  • Regulatory compliance
  • Key performance indicators
  • Experimental design
  • Uplift analysis
  • Return on investment analysis
  • Business analytics
  • Large language models

Experience with modern data and AI tools can also be beneficial.

Examples mentioned in the opportunity include:

  • AWS
  • CoPilot
  • Snowflake
  • Databricks
  • LLM technologies

Applicants do not necessarily need to have experience with every technology listed above. The announcement distinguishes these capabilities as preferred qualifications rather than the core eligibility requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Although the required qualifications establish the basic eligibility criteria, JPMorganChase also identifies several preferred skills.

A strong candidate may demonstrate knowledge or experience in:

Machine Learning and Data Science

Applicants should ideally have a strong understanding of data science and machine learning principles.

Experience working with complex datasets can be particularly relevant.

Programming

Knowledge of programming languages such as:

  • Python
  • SQL

can be valuable for data analysis and data-related projects.

Artificial Intelligence Tools

Experience using contemporary data and AI technologies can also strengthen an application.

Examples include:

  • AWS
  • Microsoft Copilot
  • Snowflake
  • Databricks
  • Large language models

Data Governance

Applicants with an understanding of data management and governance may be well aligned with the role.

Relevant concepts include:

  • Data platforms
  • Data pipelines
  • Data models
  • Taxonomies
  • Metadata
  • Data lineage
  • Privacy
  • Regulatory compliance

Quantitative Problem-Solving

The role requires strong analytical thinking.

Applicants should be able to use quantitative methods to:

  • Design experiments
  • Evaluate results
  • Develop key performance indicators
  • Measure uplift
  • Analyze return on investment
  • Identify patterns
  • Develop evidence-based recommendations

Communication

Technical knowledge alone is not sufficient.

The role also requires the ability to communicate technical findings clearly to business stakeholders.

Applicants should be able to explain analytical work in a way that people without a highly technical background can understand.

Turning Business Problems Into Data Solutions

An important aspect of the Data & AI Program is the ability to translate business objectives into analytical problems.

This means that interns may need to understand a business or organizational challenge and then determine:

  1. What question needs to be answered?
  2. What data is required?
  3. How should the data be analyzed?
  4. What hypothesis can be tested?
  5. What model or experiment should be developed?
  6. What results would indicate success?
  7. What recommendations can be made based on the evidence?

This combination of technical and business thinking is an important component of modern data and AI roles.

Networking and Professional Development

The Data for Good Hackathon is not only a technical competition-style experience.

It also provides participants with opportunities to interact with:

  • JPMorganChase data professionals
  • Artificial intelligence professionals
  • Technology professionals
  • Recruiters
  • Other students
  • Aspiring data and AI professionals
  • Professionals involved in social-impact technology

Participants can use these interactions to learn more about technology careers within financial services and better understand the types of skills organizations are seeking in data and AI professionals.

Training, Mentorship and Access to Leaders

The program description highlights opportunities for professional development through:

  • Ongoing training
  • Mentorship
  • Access to senior leaders
  • Collaboration with experienced technologists
  • Agile team experience
  • Exposure to real-world projects

These experiences can help students better understand how technical teams operate in a large global organization.

Internship Locations

The potential locations listed for the 2027 Data & AI Program Summer Internship include:

  • Chicago, Illinois
  • Columbus, Ohio
  • Plano, Texas
  • New York Metro
  • Delaware Metro

The job posting also lists specific locations associated with the broader position:

  • Chicago, Illinois
  • Columbus, Ohio
  • Wilmington, Delaware
  • Plano, Texas
  • New York, New York
  • Jersey City, New Jersey
  • Palo Alto, California
  • Newark, Delaware

However, the announcement specifically notes that the above locations are associated with the internship program and should not be confused with the location of the Data for Good Hackathon.

Data for Good Hackathon Location and Date

The Data for Good Hackathon itself will be held at the JPMorganChase Brooklyn office in New York.

Hackathon Date

Friday, October 16 – Saturday, October 17, 2026

Applicants should distinguish this event date from the 2027 Summer Internship, which is the potential subsequent opportunity.

Application Deadline

The job posting states an application closing date of:

October 12, 2026 at 06:59 AM

The Data for Good Hackathon details also state:

Friday, October 16, 2026 at 12:00 AM Eastern Time

Because the posting contains two different deadline references, applicants should verify the deadline shown in the live JPMorganChase application portal and submit their application as early as possible.

JPMorganChase states that internship classes are filled on a rolling basis, so waiting until the final deadline may not be advisable.

How to Apply

Applicants interested in the Data for Good Hackathon are instructed to complete several steps.

Step 1: Read the Official Rules

Before beginning the application, applicants should carefully review the official rules and candidate agreement associated with the Data for Good Hackathon.

The official rules should be used to understand the conditions and requirements associated with participation.

Step 2: Submit a Complete Application

Applicants should complete the application carefully and provide a resume.

The application and resume are important because they provide the recruitment team with an initial understanding of the applicant’s:

  • Academic background
  • Technical skills
  • Projects
  • Experience
  • Interests
  • Relevant accomplishments

Applicants should ensure that all relevant questions are answered completely.

Step 3: Select Preferred JPMorganChase Locations

Applicants will be asked to indicate which JPMorganChase locations they are most interested in learning about.

Selected applicants may then be invited to participate in a hackathon with technologists and recruiters associated with their preferred work location.

Step 4: Application Review

After submission, JPMorganChase will review applications to determine whether applicants meet the required qualifications.

Step 5: Selection Notification

Selected applicants will receive an email containing additional information and final event details.

Step 6: Bring a Laptop

Participants are expected to bring their own laptops to the hackathon.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they have access to a suitable computer for the technical activities involved in the event.

Travel Expenses

The opportunity states that travel expenses may be covered under certain conditions for the two-day Data for Good experience.

Applicants should review the official event information carefully for the specific conditions governing travel support.

The provided announcement does not establish that all travel, accommodation, or other expenses will automatically be covered for every participant.

Salary Information

The posting provides the following base pay information for the position:

  • Chicago, Illinois: $95,000
  • New York, New York: $110,000–$115,000
  • Jersey City, New Jersey: $110,000–$115,000
  • Palo Alto, California: $110,000–$115,000

The salary figures provided in the announcement are associated with the position and location and should not be interpreted as a universal salary applicable to every location or circumstance.

Inclusive Workplace

JPMorganChase states that it is committed to creating an inclusive work environment that respects people for their individual skills, backgrounds, and professional experiences.

The company also states that it provides reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities.

Applicants who require accommodations should use the appropriate JPMorganChase recruitment channels to request support during the application process.

Important Considerations for International Students

The permanent U.S. work-authorization requirement is one of the most important aspects of this opportunity.

Students who are studying in the United States but would require employer sponsorship should not assume that their current student status automatically satisfies the requirement.

JPMorganChase explicitly states that it does not provide employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program and will not provide assistance or documentation supporting OPT, CPT, or other immigration sponsorship or benefits.

Applicants should therefore verify their eligibility based on their specific U.S. work authorization before applying.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to students who are:

  • Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree
  • Studying data science, computer science, mathematics, machine learning, or another quantitative/technical discipline
  • Graduating between December 2027 and August 2028
  • Interested in artificial intelligence and machine learning
  • Interested in data analytics
  • Comfortable working with quantitative information
  • Developing Python or SQL skills
  • Interested in social-impact technology
  • Interested in financial services technology
  • Interested in solving real-world problems using data
  • Interested in collaborative technology projects
  • Authorized to work permanently in the United States

Students do not need to have previous professional work experience to meet the stated experience requirement.

What Makes the Opportunity Relevant to Data and AI Students?

The opportunity connects academic technical knowledge with practical applications.

Instead of working exclusively on classroom exercises, participants can apply their skills to datasets and challenges connected to real nonprofit organizations.

This can provide exposure to several aspects of the modern data lifecycle, including:

Data → Analysis → Modeling → Insights → Recommendations → Impact

The experience can also help participants understand how technical work needs to connect with stakeholder objectives and measurable outcomes.

Click HERE  to read more.

Preparing a Strong Application

Students interested in applying can strengthen their application by presenting their technical experience clearly.

Relevant experience can include:

  • University data science projects
  • Machine learning projects
  • Python projects
  • SQL projects
  • Artificial intelligence projects
  • Data visualization
  • Research involving quantitative analysis
  • Kaggle or similar data projects
  • Hackathons
  • Open-source contributions
  • Academic research
  • Projects involving large datasets
  • Analytics dashboards
  • AI or machine learning experiments

Applicants should focus on demonstrating what they actually built, analyzed, or achieved rather than simply listing technologies.

For example, instead of only stating that they know Python, applicants can describe a project where they used Python to clean a dataset, develop a model, conduct an analysis, or generate recommendations.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The JPMorganChase Data for Good Hackathon offers eligible students an opportunity to apply data and AI skills to real-world social-impact challenges while working alongside experienced technology professionals.

The two-day hackathon in Brooklyn, New York, is particularly relevant to students studying data science, machine learning, computer science, mathematics, and related quantitative disciplines.

Beyond the hackathon, participants may have an opportunity to learn more about and be considered for the 2027 Data & AI Program Summer Internship. The internship provides exposure to data analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, data platforms, governance, business problem-solving, and collaborative technology projects.

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements, particularly the December 2027–August 2028 graduation window and the requirement to be permanently authorized to work in the United States. The company does not provide employment-based immigration sponsorship or support for OPT/CPT for this program.

The application should be completed carefully and submitted as early as possible because JPMorganChase states that internship positions are filled on a rolling basis.

For students who meet the requirements, the opportunity combines social-impact technology, data and AI, professional networking, mentorship, practical problem-solving, and potential exposure to a major financial-services technology career pathway.

Click HERE for more internship opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The WiSER Pioneers Program 2026 is a year-long leadership and professional development opportunity designed to equip young women with the skills, knowledge, confidence and professional networks needed to contribute to the global energy transformation and sustainable development.

Through mentorship, leadership training, educational workshops and global networking opportunities, participants can develop their professional capabilities while connecting with other women who are passionate about sustainability and positive change.

The program provides an opportunity for young women to transform their passion for sustainability into meaningful action and long-term professional impact within their communities and beyond.

About the WiSER Pioneers Program

The WiSER Pioneers Program is an initiative under Women in Sustainability, Environment and Renewable Energy (WiSER), a platform associated with Masdar.

The program focuses on developing the next generation of women leaders who can contribute to sustainability, environmental development, renewable energy, energy transition and related areas.

The year-long program combines professional development, mentorship, networking and educational activities. Participants have opportunities to learn from experienced professionals, interact with other emerging women leaders and gain broader exposure to global sustainability issues.

WiSER has built an international community of women from different countries and professional backgrounds who are interested in sustainability and the global energy transition.

What Does the WiSER Pioneers Program Offer?

The program provides participants with several opportunities for professional and personal development.

1. Leadership Development

Participants receive opportunities to strengthen their leadership skills and develop the confidence required to take on greater responsibilities in their careers and communities.

Leadership development is an important component of the program because sustainability challenges require individuals who can communicate ideas, collaborate effectively and contribute to practical solutions.

2. Mentorship

Mentorship is another important component of the WiSER experience.

Participants have opportunities to learn from experienced professionals and leaders. Mentorship can provide valuable career insights, guidance on professional development and a better understanding of opportunities and challenges within sustainability-related industries.

3. Educational Workshops

Participants can take part in educational workshops focused on sustainability, energy, environmental issues and related subjects.

These workshops allow participants to expand their knowledge, learn from experts and explore issues that are relevant to the rapidly changing global energy and sustainability landscape.

4. Global Networking

The WiSER Pioneers Program provides participants with access to an international network of women professionals.

Participants can use this network to:

  • Meet women from different countries and professional backgrounds
  • Exchange ideas and experiences
  • Build international professional relationships
  • Explore potential collaborations
  • Learn about sustainability initiatives around the world
  • Develop a broader understanding of global sustainability challenges

5. Exposure to Industry Experts

Participants can gain exposure to professionals and experts working in sustainability, energy, environmental development and related sectors.

This exposure can help participants understand how sustainability principles are being applied in real-world professional environments.

6. Community Impact

The program encourages participants to use the knowledge and experience they gain to contribute to positive change within their communities and beyond.

The objective is not only to support individual career development but also to encourage participants to become active contributors to sustainability and the global energy transition.

Program Duration and Commitment

The WiSER Pioneers Program is designed to run for one year.

Because of the length of the program, successful participants are expected to make a meaningful commitment throughout the program period.

Participants are expected to:

  • Attend scheduled workshops and events
  • Participate actively in WiSER activities
  • Attend at least 70% of scheduled workshops and events
  • Participate in Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week
  • Participate in the Annual WiSER Forum
  • Engage with other members of the WiSER community
  • Provide feedback through surveys and other program activities
  • Promote the program through their professional or social networks when applicable

Applicants should therefore consider their availability and professional commitments before applying.

Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week

Participants are expected to participate in Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week, an international platform that brings together leaders, experts, businesses, policymakers and other stakeholders to discuss sustainability and sustainable development.

Participation can give WiSER Pioneers greater exposure to international sustainability discussions and professionals working across different sectors.

Annual WiSER Forum

The Annual WiSER Forum is another important component of the WiSER experience.

The forum provides opportunities for participants to interact with sustainability leaders, experts and other members of the WiSER community.

It also provides an environment where participants can exchange ideas and gain exposure to emerging developments in sustainability, energy and environmental leadership.

Who Can Apply?

The WiSER Pioneers Program is designed specifically for young women who are developing professional careers in sustainability, environment, energy, STEM and related areas.

Applicants should meet the relevant eligibility requirements, including:

  • Be a woman
  • Be between 25 and 35 years old
  • Hold a relevant bachelor’s degree
  • Have at least two years of professional experience
  • Be currently employed or self-employed
  • Have relevant experience in sustainability, environment, energy or STEM-related fields
  • Have excellent spoken English

The program is international, allowing eligible women from different countries and regions to apply.

Relevant Academic Backgrounds

The opportunity is particularly relevant to applicants with academic backgrounds connected to:

  • Sustainability
  • Environmental science
  • Environmental management
  • Renewable energy
  • Energy
  • Engineering
  • Science
  • Technology
  • Mathematics
  • Other relevant STEM disciplines

Applicants should ensure that their academic qualifications and professional experience are relevant to the focus of the program.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to provide personal and professional information through the online application form.

The application includes fields for:

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Personal contact email
  • Professional contact email
  • Nationality
  • Country of residence
  • Bachelor’s degree or major
  • Date of birth

Applicants should provide accurate and complete information when completing the application.

Mandatory 90-Second Video

One of the key application requirements is a 90-second video in English.

Applicants can either record the video directly through the application platform or upload a YouTube link.

The video must respond to the following questions:

  1. Why do you want to join the WiSER Pioneers Program?
  2. Why are you interested in sustainability? Which sustainability goal are you most passionate about, and why?
  3. What are some of your key skills, insights or talents that will help you to be successful in the program?

Because the video is limited to 90 seconds, applicants should make their responses clear, focused and relevant.

Optional Written Questions

Applicants can also provide additional information through three optional written questions.

Each response has a maximum limit of 150 words.

Question 1: Motivation

Why do you want to join the WiSER Pioneers Program?

Applicants can explain their motivation for joining the program and how participation relates to their professional aspirations.

Question 2: Sustainability Interest

Why are you interested in the field of sustainability? Which sustainability goal are you most passionate about, and why?

Applicants can discuss their sustainability interests and explain the particular Sustainable Development Goal or sustainability issue that is most important to them.

Question 3: Skills and Talents

What are some of your key skills, insights or talents that will help you to be successful in the program?

Applicants can highlight their professional experience, leadership capabilities, communication skills, technical knowledge, problem-solving abilities and other qualities that could contribute to their success.

Why Apply for the WiSER Pioneers Program?

The global transition toward cleaner energy and sustainable development requires professionals with strong knowledge, leadership capabilities and the ability to collaborate across sectors and cultures.

The WiSER Pioneers Program provides a platform for young women who want to develop these capabilities.

Participants can gain access to:

  • Leadership development
  • Mentorship
  • Professional networking
  • Global exposure
  • Sustainability-focused learning
  • Connections with industry experts
  • Interaction with other women leaders
  • Opportunities to broaden professional perspectives
  • Exposure to the global energy transition
  • Opportunities to contribute to sustainability-focused initiatives

The Importance of Sustainability

Sustainability has become an important area across industries, economies and communities.

Issues such as climate change, renewable energy, energy security, environmental protection, resource efficiency and sustainable economic development require professionals who can develop practical solutions and collaborate effectively.

The WiSER Pioneers Program is designed to help young women strengthen their ability to contribute to these challenges.

The program encourages participants to connect their professional interests with broader sustainability objectives and consider how they can create meaningful impact in their communities and professional environments.

Building a Global Community of Women Leaders

One of the major features of the WiSER Pioneers Program is its international community.

Participants have the opportunity to interact with women from different nationalities, cultures and professional backgrounds.

This international environment can help participants:

  • Learn from different perspectives
  • Exchange professional experiences
  • Understand sustainability challenges in different regions
  • Build international relationships
  • Explore potential collaborations
  • Develop a stronger global perspective

WiSER’s Pioneers community has included women representing numerous nationalities, making the program particularly relevant for applicants interested in international sustainability networks.

Application Process

Applicants interested in the WiSER Pioneers Program should complete the online application form and provide all required information.

The application process includes:

  1. Completing the personal information section.
  2. Selecting nationality and country of residence.
  3. Providing bachelor’s degree or major information.
  4. Providing date-of-birth information.
  5. Completing the mandatory 90-second English video.
  6. Answering the optional written questions if desired.
  7. Reviewing all information provided.
  8. Agreeing to the applicable terms and conditions.
  9. Submitting the completed application.

Applicants should carefully review their application before submitting it to ensure that all mandatory fields and requirements have been completed.

Deadline

The application information provided does not state a specific closing date.

Applicants are advised to check the official WiSER/Masdar application portal for the latest deadline and application status before submitting their application.

Application Link

Apply for the WiSER Pioneers Program 2026

OFY Website

Visit HERE for more fellowship programs

Opportunity Category

Category: Fellowship / Leadership Development Program

The WiSER Pioneers Program is a year-long professional development and leadership program with fellowship-style characteristics. It is not a conventional scholarship, internship, job, grant or competition.

Who Qualifies for the WiSER Pioneers Program?

The opportunity is intended for:

  • Women aged 25–35
  • Applicants with a relevant bachelor’s degree
  • Applicants with at least two years of professional experience
  • Applicants who are currently employed or self-employed
  • Professionals working in or connected to sustainability, environment, energy or STEM-related areas
  • Applicants with excellent spoken English

Eligible Countries and Regions

The WiSER Pioneers Program is presented as a global opportunity and is not restricted to one particular country or continent.

Eligible women from countries around the world can apply, provided they meet the program’s stated eligibility requirements.

Conclusion

The WiSER Pioneers Program 2026 provides a year-long platform for young women who want to strengthen their leadership abilities, expand their professional networks and contribute to sustainability and the global energy transformation.

Through mentorship, educational workshops, networking, global exposure and participation in major sustainability events, participants can develop valuable knowledge, professional relationships and leadership capabilities.

The program is particularly relevant to women aged 25 to 35 who have relevant academic qualifications and professional experience in sustainability, environment, energy, STEM or related areas.

Women who are passionate about sustainability and interested in becoming part of an international community of emerging leaders can consider applying for the WiSER Pioneers Program 2026.

Category: Fellowship / Leadership Development Program

Eligible applicants: Women aged 25–35 with a relevant bachelor’s degree, at least two years of professional experience, current employment or self-employment, and excellent spoken English.

Eligible countries/regions: Global; eligible applicants from countries around the world can apply.

Deadline: Not specified in the application information provided.
